This is a mature AWS Glue/PySpark data-lakehouse project (S3 raw -> Glue ETL with an 11-rule data-quality quarantine -> partitioned Parquet -> Athena SQL, deployed via CloudFormation) already CI-green with an existing pytest suite. Checked Tier 1 first: grepped src/, glue_jobs/, and scripts/ for bare excepts, hardcoded secrets/AWS keys, and TODO/FIXME markers -- none found; reviewed scripts/deploy.sh for secrets -- none, uses AWS CLI profile/env var defaults correctly. No .env.example gap: the code reads no environment variables anywhere (AWS config flows through CloudFormation parameters and Glue job arguments, not os.environ). No Dockerfile gap: this is a batch Glue ETL job deployed via CloudFormation, not a long-running service, so a Dockerfile would not fit the architecture -- not manufactured. Tier 2 (tests) already substantial and passing in CI (Spark-based pytest suite with fixtures). Tier 3 (code quality) had a genuine gap: an AST scan of every non-test .py file found 11 public functions missing docstrings (scripts/make_charts.py: hourly/monthly/stations; scripts/run_local.py: main; scripts/run_queries.py: to_duckdb/connect/run_all; src/divvy_lakehouse/ingest.py: check_header/raw_key/main; src/divvy_lakehouse/transform.py: split_valid_invalid) and 3 missing return annotations (the three make_charts.py functions). Fixed all of them, one commit per file (5 commits). Deliberately left print() statements in ingest.py main(), run_local.py, run_queries.py, make_charts.py, and glue_jobs/raw_to_curated.py alone: these are the intentional narrated CLI/Glue-job output of standalone scripts (progress messages like "1) Ingest...", final run-metrics JSON), not debug prints in library code with callers -- converting them to logging would degrade the designed UX for no real benefit, so this was treated as not a genuine Tier 3 gap rather than manufactured busywork. Re-ran the AST scan after all five fixes: zero missing docstrings/annotations remain across the whole non-test codebase. No functions over 50 lines found. Tier 4 (CI/README/Dockerfile/.env.example) and Tier 5 (performance) already clean, not touched.
